newsitem.title: UK: Dlr steady but subdued below 1.73 marks in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dlr steady but subdued below 1.73 marks in Europe.

text.p: LONDON, Apr 16 Reuter) - The dollar made a muted start to the European session, steady below 1.73 marks after profit-taking overnight knocked it back from Tuesday's fresh 37-month high of 1.7375 marks.

Tuesday's surge in the Dow and U.S. Treasury markets on benign U.S. CPI data failed to hold the dollar above 1.73, but dealers said the dollar still looked well-supported and speculation of higher U.S. rates was still in place.
"The Dow and bonds surge was purely a domestic reaction to the soft CPI data and seemed a more technical correction of its recent falls," said a Japanese bank dealer.
Analysts said the Bundesbank's April monthly report held few surprises, which cited strong U.S. fundamentals for dollar strength and showed little opposition to the higher dollar/mark.

The report did say that mark investment and its role as a reserve currency remained strong despite uncertainty over Europe's economic and monetary union. Strict adherence to the EMU criteria was needed for a smooth transition of this role and to ensure credibility of the euro, said the report.
Dollar/mark was trading at 1.7253/63 at 0806 GMT against 1.7318/23 marks late Tuesday in Europe.
Against the yen, the dollar orbited the 126 yen level in morning Europe, down from overnight levels amid ongoing concerns of Bank of Japan intervention.
Comments overnight from senior Ministry of Finance official Eisuke Sakakibara further dampened dollar/yen upside.

As well as reiterating official concerns over excessive forex moves, Sakakibara highlighted the divergence of economic fundamentals with the dollar/yen rate over the last few weeks and said the weak yen was not due to the U.S./Japan interest rate differential.

"This is still part of the process of Japanese officials expressing their unhappiness with the speed of the decline of the yen," said Roger Francis, senior analyst at IBJ International. "But what he is saying is broadly true."
Sakakibara was implying the market was overshooting in its pessimism of the Japanese economy and the low rate environment was seeing the economy growing quickly, said IBJ's Francis.
Dollar/yen was trading at 126.00/10 against 126.23/33 late Monday in Europe.
Sakakibara is scheduled to speak today sometime after 0930 GMT.
Market focus today was on U.S. March industrial production and capacity utilisation data due at 1315 GMT.
Also on today's agenda was an Economic Strategy Institute trade policy conference in Washington with U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky speaking.
Though analysts expected little concrete from the conference, it comes before the release of Japanese trade data tonight and U.S. trade numbers Thursday.
